text:
Frink
 

 
 
 
 
 

 
 Desktop-first app for parallel agents and triggered multi-step workflows. 
 Workflows can include steps you write yourself in code, alongside agent, command and approval steps.
 

 
 Save a routine as a Flow and it starts by itself: on a schedule, from any webhook, or from an event in Linear, Shortcut, ClickUp, Sentry, PostHog or Vercel. 
 Finished work and agent questions wait for you in the Work Queue, on your computer or on your iPhone (beta). 
 It all runs on your computer while Frink is open, with the AI coding tool you already use. No Frink account.
 

 Download Frink 

 
 
 

 Features

 
 
 

 Run four agents side by side

Split the window into up to four panes and give each agent a different job. They work at the same time, and each pane keeps its own model and its own diff to review. Put each one on its own git worktree and they never touch the same files.

Docs →

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 One sentence becomes an automation

Type the routine the way you would say it: "Every weekday at 9am, run the tests. If any fail, have an agent fix them, then wait for my approval before it opens a PR." Frink builds it as a Flow and lists every step, so you can read it and change it before it runs.

Docs →

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 It starts when something happens

A new ticket in Linear, Shortcut or ClickUp, an error in Sentry, an event in PostHog or Vercel, any webhook, or a time of day. The Flow checks a condition to pick its path, and waits at an approval step until you say yes.

Docs →

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Everything that needs you, in one queue

Every run from every project shows up in the Work Queue as running, ready for review or queued. A badge appears when a Flow stops for approval or an agent has a question. Read what it did, then approve it or reply to send it back.

Docs →

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Check the work and fix it yourself

Every file the agent changes shows as a diff. Open it in the built-in editor, change a line and save, run a command in the terminal, or roll the chat and its code back to an earlier point.

Docs →

 
 
 
 
 
 

 Also in the box: 

- Custom steps — need a step Frink doesn't have? Ask the agent to write one in JavaScript, or write it yourself, and reuse it in any Flow. For another language, use a command step.
- Plugins & MCP — connect Linear, Shortcut, ClickUp, GitHub, Notion, Slack, Sentry, PostHog and more, as chat tools and Flow steps.
- Your own AI sign-in — uses your existing Claude Code or Codex login, the OpenCode or GitHub Copilot you installed, or your Cursor sign-in. Frink only checks that you are signed in and leaves the login with the tool. If you paste an Anthropic API key instead, it is stored encrypted on your computer.
- Local-first — chats, Flows and tasks live in SQLite on your machine. No account needed. Official builds send anonymous usage counts and crash reports: everything Frink sends.

---

 Supported Agents

 
 Claude Code  
 Codex  
 OpenCode  
 GitHub Copilot  
 Cursor 
 

Bring your own subscription or API key — Frink runs the agent, you keep the account.

---

 Install

- Download from frink.dev 
- Or grab a build directly: macOS Apple Silicon · macOS Intel
- Or build from source — see CONTRIBUTING.md.

 Linux (x64 and arm64)

Download the AppImage or the .deb from frink.dev/download, or directly: x64 AppImage · .deb, arm64 AppImage · .deb. Both update themselves.

- AppImage (any distro): chmod +x Frink-X.Y.Z.AppImage && ./Frink-X.Y.Z.AppImage , with X.Y.Z the version you downloaded. It does not need libfuse2: it mounts itself with fusermount3 from the fuse3 package. If it will not start, install fuse3 or start it with --appimage-extract-and-run . Keep it in a folder you can write to, such as /Applications , so updates can replace it.
- .deb (Debian/Ubuntu): sudo apt install ./frink X.Y.Z amd64.deb ( arm64.deb on arm64). Updates ask for your password in a system prompt.

Frink saves API keys and MCP credentials only when it can encrypt them with a desktop keyring (GNOME Keyring or KWallet). Without one it does not save them, so install one and relaunch Frink before adding accounts.

---

 Community & Support

- Bugs & ideas: open an issue.
- Changelog: frink.dev/changelog.
- Show support: star the repo to follow along.

---

 Developing

Want to contribute or run locally? See our CONTRIBUTING.md guide.
